change: Single kernel: the query (term, weight) list is a by-value kernel argument, and the last range block to finish merges all ranges' lists (threadfence + atomic ticket; counter reset by that block). The merge is the multi-warp pattern from variant 1 run by the block's own threads.
justification_from_profile: 20261114-cuda5-profile-01: merge kernel 9.3% of GPU kernel time on a single block; four GPU operations per query (2 kernels, 2 copies) with the GPU idle about 17% of each query's span between them.
behaviour_deltas_vs_variant_3: Per query: 1 kernel launch and 1 device-to-host copy (was 2 launches, 1 host-to-device and 1 device-to-host copy).
Kernel argument grows by a 1,028-byte QueryArgs struct (128 terms).
The merge uses the scoring kernel's thread count; MERGE_THREADS must equal SCORE_THREADS and is otherwise unused.
A 4-byte device counter must be 0 before every launch; the driver zeroes it once and the last block re-arms it.
review_before_running: Ordering: each thread executes __threadfence after its candidate writes; the following barrier means every thread of the block has fenced; only then does thread 0 take the ticket. A block observing ticket == ranges-1 therefore runs after every other block's fenced writes.
Exactly one block sees the final ticket; is_last is written by thread 0 and read by all threads after a barrier.
The merge reuses warp_length after all of this block's earlier reads of it (a barrier separates them); heads and scratch are touched only by the merging block.
The counter is reset after the merge by the same block; launches are sequential on one stream, so the next launch starts from 0.
checks: Fixtures with --encoding positions --single-kernel (216 scorer runs with 1 to 8,292 range blocks, 10 rejections); 100K/1M x 500 queries x k=10/1000 x 2 passes with zero mismatches.
validation_limits: If a launch were aborted mid-kernel the counter would stay non-zero and later launches would not merge; the driver does not detect this beyond its per-result validity and order checks. Not observed.
Launches must not overlap (one stream, batch 1).
